content.title: About
content.content: Black tea is a fully fermented leaf tea made from the dried leaves of Camellia sinensis. It has a rich aroma, robust flavor, and a characteristic amber‑colored infusion. Black tea is most commonly served hot, but it can also be used in cold beverages.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black tea is the most widely consumed type of tea worldwide.
The term “black” refers to the color of the dried leaves, not the brewed liquid.
Afternoon tea in England originated in the early 19th century.
The most expensive black tea is Da Hong Pao, cultivated in China.
Black tea contains theaflavins and thearubigins formed during fermentation.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Flavonoids in black tea improve vascular function and may reduce the risk of heart disease.

items.title: Enhanced focus
items.content: Caffeine together with L‑theanine boosts attention and cognitive performance without a sharp energy spike.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Theaflavins and thearubigins provide strong antioxidant activity, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: A warm infusion can soothe digestive discomfort and promote normal gut motility.

items.title: Reduced risk of type 2 diabetes
items.content: Regular moderate consumption of black tea is linked to improved insulin sensitivity.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat with excessive intake.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Tea can enhance the effect of certain anticoagulants and reduce the absorption of iron supplements.

items.title: Tannin content
items.content: Tannins may lower the absorption of non‑heme iron, so it’s best to drink tea between meals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Place 1‑2 tsp of loose leaves in hot water (90‑95 °C) and steep for 3‑5 minutes. Add milk, lemon, honey, or spices to taste. Black tea also serves as a base for iced drinks and cocktails.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store loose‑leaf black tea in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Keep it away from moisture and strong odors to preserve its flavor and aroma.
